format64-exact.what: FL_EXACT for every binary64 x in place of every binary32 x: attacks the reasoning (only binary32 numbers of magnitude 2^23 or more are whole). KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: ext-work/p1/plant-facts-run1.txt, Python binary64: x = 2^23 + 1/2 is binary64, the graph returns it, and floor x is a whole number. Refused in the 2^23 branch, where the proof needs the input it returns to be a binary32 number (measured, rehearsal r1)

no-step.what: the zero step removed from the graph and the shape alike (the kernel still accepts FL_model). Attacks the reasoning about the sign of a zero. KNOWN FALSE (FL_SIGN): at x = -0 the unstepped shape gives +0, MEASURED: ext-work/p1/plant-facts-run1.txt, Python binary64; and ext-work/p1/probe/probe-plant-run1.txt (C, all 2^32 inputs). Refused where the proof needs the step (the model lemma that the step changes no value)

sign-always-plus.what: FL_SIGN claims every result has sign bit 0. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: ext-work/p1/plant-facts-run1.txt, Python binary64: at x = -1 the result is -1. Refused in the proof of FL_SIGN

ieee-other-mode.what: FL_IEEE with Bnearbyint at mode_UP for mode_DN. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: ext-work/p1/plant-facts-run1.txt, Python binary64: at x = 1/2 the two differ. THE TRUST BOUNDARY: Floor32.v (the four other parts) compiles with this statement; the refusal is in FloorIEEE.v alone

value-no-finite.what: FL_VALUE without the premise that the input is finite. KNOWN FALSE, MEASURED: ext-work/p1/plant-facts-run1.txt, Python binary64: at +infinity (B2R is 0, a binary32 number) the result is +infinity, not finite. Refused where the proof takes the premise

admitted.what: fl_floor_near (floor from the nearest whole number) ends with Admitted

mul0-axiom.what: fl_mul0 (b * +0 for a finite b is the zero with the sign of b) is an Axiom of the same statement, its proof removed; used by the top theorem through the step lemmas

four-of-five.what: Closed.v states, under the name FLOOR32, four of the five parts (FL_IEEE left out) and proves that
